requirement: EPIC 1 Story 2 — while playing, queue pattern selection and atomically swap audio, grid, and active-slot state at the next loop boundary; rapid choices are latest-wins.
story: Net tracker: EPIC 1 #2 — Queue loop-boundary swap (High, Priority 3).

architecture.decision: The story is implemented by the committed usePatternBank/useTransportEngine seam from EPIC 1 Story 1: commitQueuedSlot swaps activePatternRef synchronously at s === 0 inside the existing onStepAudio subscriber, before the pattern is read for scheduling; React active-slot state follows in the same tick.
alternatives: Switch in the visual onStep callback: rejected because it runs after audio scheduling.
Register a separate audio subscriber for switching: rejected because correctness would depend on Set insertion order.
tradeoffs: Story 1 introduced the full seam so authoring and playback could share one bank; Story 2 adds no duplicate implementation.
The selected slot is visible as queued immediately, while the active slot remains unchanged until step 0.
seams: src/hooks/usePatternBank.ts owns queuedSlotRef, activePatternRef, and commitQueuedSlot.
src/hooks/useTransportEngine.ts calls commitQueuedSlot as the first operation inside onStepAudio when s === 0.
The existing transport callback order fires audio subscribers before visual subscribers.

tasks.title: Audit the committed boundary-swap seam
tasks.intent: Confirm the implementation matches the locked F4 ordering and that latest queued selection is the only state committed at the loop boundary.
tasks.constraints: Do not move switching to visual onStep, add a second subscriber, or introduce another audio engine; preserve synchronous ref replacement and no-op behavior when nothing is queued.
tasks.acceptance: The bank owns active/queued refs; commitQueuedSlot clears the queue, changes active state/ref together, and the audio callback invokes it before reading patternRef.current at s === 0.
tasks.result: Audit passed in commit fb71041: commitQueuedSlot updates refs/state before the pattern read; queuedSlotRef gives latest-wins semantics; transport audio subscribers precede visual subscribers.

tasks.title: Run build and regression checks
tasks.intent: Ensure the boundary implementation remains type-safe and does not regress the four-slot persistence or UI integration.
tasks.constraints: Preserve unrelated app-screenshot.png; no code changes unless a real gate failure appears.
tasks.acceptance: Diff check and production build pass with no TypeScript errors.
tasks.result: Build and diff gates passed; the existing committed bank/transport implementation remains type-safe and preserves four-slot integration.

tasks.title: Verify stopped, queued, and latest-wins playback behavior
tasks.intent: Prove the player-facing acceptance in the running browser, including actual transport playback and zero runtime errors.
tasks.constraints: Start the real transport; verify stopped selection is immediate, playing selection leaves active state unchanged until the boundary, rapid 2→3→4 activates only 4, and audio/grid/active state update together.
tasks.acceptance: Browser checks pass for immediate stopped switching, visible queued state, next-boundary activation, latest-wins selection, and no console errors.
tasks.visual: Run the Vite app, inspect the slot controls, start playback, queue 2→3→4, observe queued 4 then active 4 after the step-0 boundary, and capture evidence.
tasks.result: Browser acceptance passed: stopped selection changed immediately; real transport playback kept active 1 while showing Queued 4 after rapid 2→3→4; the next loop boundary activated slot 4 and cleared the queue; playback stopped cleanly with zero console errors.
evidence: Browser stopped selection: active slot 2 then active slot 1
Browser pre-boundary: Queued 2 · active 1 and then Queued 4 · active 1
Browser post-boundary: active slot 4 and no queued status
Browser screenshots captured before and after the boundary
